Ruth Calder
Born1938, Duluth, Minnesota
OccupationNurse
SpouseWalt (met 1959)
ParentsHenrik Calder
SiblingsJune Calder Moe; Pete
RelativesAnders Calder (grandfather)

Ruth Calder (born 1938) is the subject of this demonstration lineage, an invented family used to show what Lineage does. She grew up in Duluth, Minnesota, trained as a nurse in Minneapolis, and with her husband Walt built a cabin on Pike Lake.[1][2]

Contents
  1. Early life
  2. Nursing and marriage
  3. Pike Lake
  4. In the family's memory
  5. In the stories

Early life

Ruth was born in Duluth in 1938, the daughter of Henrik Calder, who worked at the ore docks.[3][4] When she was "maybe seven or eight" she carried her father's lunch to the dock in a tin pail; the dock was so tall "you had to tip your head all the way back."[1] In November 1950 a great snowfall closed her school for a week, and she and her brother Pete dug a tunnel from the porch to the street; the Duluth Lakeside Courier reported the closing on its front page.[5][6] Her father wrote to her from France in September 1944.[7]

Nursing and marriage

In 1956 she went to Minneapolis for three years of nursing school, living in a dormitory where the house mother inspected the students' shoes every morning.[2] She met Walt at a church dance in 1959.[8]

Pike Lake

From about 1964 Ruth and Walt built a cabin on Pike Lake over four summers. Walt built the walls and Ruth the roof, "because he was afraid of heights."[9]

In the family's memory

"The lake was always there. Whatever else happened, the lake was always there."[10]

In the stories

The Ore Dock; Walt and the Cabin.
